evidence_level: Compiled (Release runtime at the PR 157 head)
Browser exercised: one natural four-Mario CPU9 Final Destination match, 10,657 source frames, no live-match timing pause (experiment 1)
Browser exercised, induced: a second headless page occupying the GPU-process main thread produced a forced timing pause 1.12 s after the load was raised (experiment 2, one run)
Not performance admitted; not foreground, physical-input or audible; the natural cursor-1645 pause is not reproduced and its trigger remains unidentified

classification.mechanism_demonstrated_under_induced_loa: sustained GPU-process occupancy lengthens GPU completion latency; the two-slot browser staging ring then makes each catch-up draw wait for completion; callback duration feeds back into clock debt; the eight-tick guard fires
classification.host_cpu_contention: not tested (the induced schedule ended at its first pause, before the CPU-spinner window)
classification.observer_induced_pause_found: experiment 1 Results pause at source frame 532 coincides with the harness capture read, not live play

clock.fact: FixedTickClock (menu clock, Pause policy) adds elapsed wall time between callback starts as debt; more than 8 whole ticks forces a pause; a callback runs at most 8 ticks. A long callback is therefore debt for the next.

staging_ring.fact: Emscripten StagingBufferCount equals FrameSlotCount, which is 2; begin_frame waits for a slot released by OnSubmittedWorkDone, yielding with emscripten_sleep(0). One draw per source tick, so ticks beyond the second in a callback wait for GPU completion.

mechanism_source.stability_condition: derived from the ring size, not measured directly: sustained 60 Hz needs completion latency L no greater than about 2 x 16.67 ms = 33 ms with two slots; above that catch-up cost per tick exceeds one tick and the loop diverges

per_step_ratio_to_experiment_1_median.begin: about 48x (4.8 vs 0.1 ms, includes the wait)

pr_157_diagnostic_comparison.reading: PR 157 staging wait was 7% of its final callback; the induced cascade was 72%. The PR 157 pause therefore mixes GPU wait with a process-wide slowdown; GPU-process occupancy alone does not reproduce its composition.

proposed_fix.change: Give the Emscripten renderer more frames in flight on desktop (FrameSlotCount and StagingBufferCount from 2 to 4) in the downstream patch to Aurora lib/gfx/frame.hpp, so a bounded catch-up burst does not serialize on GPU completion; tolerance rises from about 33 ms to about 67 ms completion latency
proposed_fix.cost: each staging buffer is 63 MiB (24+5+2+8+24 MiB): about 126 MiB more GPU allocation, plus per-slot CPU shadows; keep 2 on mobile until #134 memory work lands, or right-size slots to used bytes
proposed_fix.keeps_source_semantics: source ticks, one draw per tick, order, arithmetic, clock threshold, audio and GPU commands are unchanged; only the number of buffers in flight changes
validation: identical per-frame submitted-byte hashes for 600 frames, ring 2 versus 4

limits: One natural run and one induced run; no distribution, no repetition.
The natural cursor-1645 four-player replay (recorded input) was not available to this checkout and was not reproduced; experiment 1 used natural CPU9 play with the same lineup, stage and build.
The trace ring wrapped; the natural match start (source frame 63) has table data but no trace.
The induced pause proves a sufficient mechanism, not that it caused the PR 157 pause; the PR 157 composition differs.
Host CPU contention, thermal state and other GPU clients were not isolated.
Headless only: no foreground timing, physical input, audible output, mobile or performance admission.
Experiment budget at this boundary (two) is spent.
